question: Triangle \(ABC\) is isosceles with base \(AC.\) Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are respectively in \(CB\) and \(AB\) and such that \(AC=AP=PQ=QB.\) The number of degrees in angle \(B\) is:
solution:
First interpret \(P\) and \(Q\) as strictly inside \(CB\) and \(AB\), respectively. Let \(\theta=\angle ABC\), and let \(\alpha\) be each base angle of the isosceles triangle \(ABC\). Then
\[
2\alpha+\theta=180^\circ.
\]
The equal lengths create smaller isosceles triangles, allowing us to express the angles at \(A\) in terms of \(\theta\).

Since \(AC=AP\), triangle \(ACP\) has equal angles at \(C\) and \(P\). Its angle at \(C\) is \(\alpha\), because \(P\) lies between \(C\) and \(B\). Therefore
\[
\angle CAP=180^\circ-2\alpha=\theta.
\]
Since \(BQ=PQ\), triangle \(BQP\) has equal angles at \(B\) and \(P\), both \(\theta\). Hence \(\angle BQP=180^\circ-2\theta\). The rays \(QA\) and \(QB\) are opposite, so \(\angle AQP=2\theta\).

Finally, \(AP=PQ\) makes triangle \(APQ\) isosceles, giving \(\angle PAQ=\angle AQP=2\theta\). Thus
\[
\alpha=\angle CAB
=\angle CAP+\angle PAB
=\theta+2\theta=3\theta.
\]
Substituting into the angle sum of \(ABC\) gives
\[
7\theta=180^\circ,
\qquad
\theta=\frac{180^\circ}{7}=25\frac57^\circ.
\]
This proves choice A under the strict-interior interpretation.

If endpoints are allowed, that interpretation matters. An equilateral triangle with \(P=C\) and \(Q=A\) satisfies \(AC=AP=PQ=QB\) and has \(\angle B=60^\circ\).

A different example has \(\angle B=36^\circ\) and base angles \(72^\circ\). Put \(P=C\), and let the bisector of \(\angle ACB\) meet \(AB\) at \(Q\). In triangle \(ACQ\), the angles at \(A\) and \(Q\) are both \(72^\circ\), so \(CQ=AC\). In triangle \(BCQ\), the angles at \(B\) and \(C\) are both \(36^\circ\), so \(BQ=CQ\). With \(P=C\), all four required lengths are therefore equal.

Thus the intended interior-point answer is \(\boxed{25\frac57^\circ}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\). If the sides are treated as closed segments, these two endpoint examples show that the angle is not determined, choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
